explanation: LanguageOptions went to Policy definition, but the dialog only edits the ADML language preference, which Main stores with Configuration.SetValue("LanguageCode") (Main.vb 809) and reads back at 478. The registry holds a Program setting entity (a remembered user preference in the app's own registry key) that fits better. Reassign it there, or state why the translation-language choice belongs with the definitions.

FilterConfiguration is an in-memory view filter (Main.vb 12, never stored). Its PolicyState and Commented fields test configured state and comments, which are not definition data. Either give a notBusinessDataReason (transient view criteria) or justify Policy definition by the fields that are catalogue data (ManagedPolicy, AllowedProducts).

FilterPolicyState (Configured, NotConfigured, Enabled, Disabled) names the configured state of a policy, which the registry puts under Policy setting, not Policy definition; it is also only a filter choice. Re-decide it with FilterConfiguration: a notBusinessDataReason or Policy setting, with reasons.
